svg.title: 04a · Resilience and Recovery: As-Is
svg.desc: Left: every component runs as a single instance on one host with no restart policy, persistent volume, replication or backup. Right: protocol-level resilience that is implemented and verified (asynchronous decoupling, expiry, idempotency, status queries, ordered positions) and capabilities that are absent. Bottom: seven failure scenarios with expected behaviour, evidence and recovery.
svg.text: Single points of failure in the harness, the resilience built into the Mojaloop protocol and services, and how each failure scenario plays out here
no restart policy · no persistent volumes · no replication · no backups
If it fails: no transfer intake and no callbacks to FSPs
If it fails: no payee discovery
API + prepare, fulfil, get, admin, timeout in one process
If it fails: transfers stop; nothing expires until it is back
If it fails: transfers stay RECEIVED_PREPARE, later
If it fails: no window close or settlement (operator task)
If it fails: all quotes and transfers stop; unconsumed
single instance · no volume · no backup
If it fails: ledger, positions, quotes, settlement stop;
container removal loses all ledger data
If it fails: lookups stop · object store / reporting stop ·
SDK Scheme Adapter + its Redis: single containers. If either fails mid-transfer the FSP loses in-flight state and must resolve the outcome with GET /transfers/{id}.
Recovery here means rebuilding (measured in the labs)
First image pull: ~11.2 GB, ~25 min · docker compose up -d of the standard stack: ~5.5 min
Golden-path provisioning: ~4 min · P2P test re-run on a warm stack: ~18 s
RESILIENCE BUILT INTO THE PROTOCOL AND SERVICES
Any data from before the rebuild is gone; there is nothing to restore from
APIs answer 202 after publishing to Kafka; handlers work independently of the caller
Every transfer has an expiration; the timeout handler (cron every 15 s) aborts it and
Same ID + same body → no double processing, current state re-sent; changed body →
GET /transfers/{id} and GET /quotes/{id} let an FSP recover after a timeout (verified, M9)
Position messages keyed by participant account; batch applied in one DB transaction
wait4 retries each dependency 60 × 10 s; 17 Compose health checks
No DLQ topics or handler configuration found
None on switch services or data stores
Single MySQL, Kafka RF 1, no volumes
Not defined anywhere: a design decision
No chaos or fault-injection tests in the repo
Verified timing hazard (M10 lab): layers time out at different moments
Payee core banking slowed to 75 s → payer SDK gave up at ~44 s → switch expired the transfer at ~62 s (3303) → the payee still credited the customer at 75 s: a reconciliation break.
Rule: every layer's timeout must be shorter than the transfer expiration.
All 31 services healthy (central-settlement shows unhealthy because of its health-check port bug); P2P test 31/31
The container stays stopped (no restart policy). Flows through it fail; reserved transfers expire once central-ledger and its timeout handler run again
Everything stops: there is one host. Containers do not come back by themselves after a host restart
Restart Docker, then the same compose command
Ledger, position, quoting and settlement writes fail. If the container is removed, all ledger data is gone (no volume, no backup)
Restart mysql; if removed, rebuild and re-run provisioning
All quotes and transfers stop; unconsumed messages are lost (RF 1, container storage). Reserved transfers later expire (3303)
All state is lost: there are no backups anywhere
Rebuild: compose up (~5.5 min) + TTK provisioning
Only a clean rebuild exists; there is no restore of earlier data
Verified: repeated down -v / up cycles in the labs
Provisioning collections recreate participants, limits and oracles
"Derived" rows follow from the configuration (no restart policy, no volumes, single instances); they were not fault-injected. The target design is 04b.
